tcf.title: TCF Canada
tcf.hubDescription: Test de connaissance du français, the French test for Canadian immigration
tcf.startDialogDescription: One full timed mock test: listening, reading, writing and speaking, in the official order.

listening.title: Listening comprehension
listening.description: 39 questions from easy to hard. Each recording plays once, with its question and choices on screen. The clock runs only while you answer, not while a recording plays.
listening.practiceDescription: Questions from easy to hard. Each recording plays once, with its question and choices on screen. The clock runs only while you answer, not while a recording plays.

reading.title: Reading comprehension
reading.description: 39 short documents, one question each. Move freely between them.
reading.practiceDescription: Short documents, one question each. Move freely between them.

writing.title: Written expression
writing.description: Three writing tasks under one shared clock. Keep to each task's word range.
writing.practiceDescription: Your writing tasks share one clock. Keep to each task's word range.

speaking.title: Oral expression
speaking.description: Three speaking tasks. Task 2 gives you 2 minutes to prepare; tasks 1 and 3 start at once.
speaking.practiceDescription: Record each task you picked. Task 2 gives you 2 minutes to prepare; tasks 1 and 3 start at once.

tcfQuebec.title: TCF Québec
tcfQuebec.hubDescription: The French test for Québec immigration (PSTQ, PEQ). On the official test you choose 1 to 4 papers, with 29 listening and 29 reading questions. Our mock runs all four skills at TCF Canada length (39 + 39 questions) and reports a CEFR level per skill.
tcfQuebec.startDialogDescription: One full timed mock of all four skills: listening, reading, writing and speaking. Listening and reading use TCF Canada's length (39 questions each, 35 and 60 min), longer than the official TCF Québec (29 questions each, 25 and 45 min). Writing (3 tasks, 60 min) and speaking (3 tasks, 12 min) have the official length.
tcfQuebec.estimateNote: Listening and reading scores are an estimate: the real TCF calibrates every question. Levels follow the official TCF scale (France Éducation international); your overall level here is your lowest skill. Québec reads each skill on its own Échelle québécoise (for example, 400–499 in listening or reading is level 7–8); PSTQ stream 1 (high qualification) and the PEQ ask for level 7 in listening and speaking and level 5 in reading and writing. Check what your file requires.
tcfQuebec.pointsFloor: On this 2013 grid, points start at B2; the two oral skills carry up to 14 of the 16, the written ones one point each. Today's PSTQ ranks French differently: up to 50 points per skill, from level 5 on the Québec scale.
tcfQuebec.pointsSource: Source: the Québec immigration points grid in force since 1 August 2013, as printed in the TCF Manuel du candidat (France Éducation international, Version Q, September 2026, p. 16). The PSTQ now uses its own French points and minimum levels, published on quebec.ca — check the grid your application is assessed on.

tcfIrn.title: TCF IRN
tcfIrn.hubDescription: The French test for a French residence card or naturalisation (Intégration, Résidence et Nationalité): four compulsory papers, 25 listening and 25 reading questions (levels up to B2). Since 1 January 2026 France asks for A2 for a first multi-year card, B1 for a first resident card (under 65) and B2 for naturalisation. Practice coming soon.
tcfIrn.startDialogDescription: One full timed mock test: listening, reading, writing and speaking, in the official order.
tcfIrn.estimateNote: Listening and reading scores are an estimate: the real TCF calibrates every question. TCF IRN scores listening and reading on a 100–499 scale, where 499 is the top of B2, and marks writing and speaking out of 20; levels follow the official TCF scale (France Éducation international). Your overall level here is your lowest skill; the official attestation counts a level as reached when three skills reach it and the fourth is at least at the top of the level below. Check the level your application requires.

celpip.mcqPoints: Each right answer is one point. A wrong answer costs nothing, so answer every question.
celpip.mcqChart: Your points become a CLB level through the chart published by Paragon, the maker of CELPIP. Listening needs a few more right answers than Reading for the same level.
celpip.mcqDifficulty: In the real test, hard questions count for more than easy ones, so the same number of right answers can land on two levels. We can't weigh question difficulty yet, so we give you the lower of the two.
celpip.mcqSlice: If you practised only some parts, your result is scaled to the full 38 questions. Part 1 is the easiest, so a level from one part is only a rough guide.
celpip.prodCriteria: An AI examiner rates each task on CELPIP's four areas: content and coherence, vocabulary, readability (writing) or listenability (speaking), and task fulfilment.
celpip.prodAverage: Your level for a section is the average of your tasks, to the nearest half. The real test is rated by trained raters and gives whole levels.
celpip.overall: It is your lowest skill. Immigration programs check each skill on its own, so your weakest skill is the one that decides.
celpip.source: Sources: Paragon Testing Enterprises, CELPIP Pro Study Packs; IRCC language test equivalency table.

tcf.mcq39: 39 questions that get harder as you go. A right answer is worth more the later it comes: from 3 points for the first, easiest questions to 33 for the last, hardest ones. Your score runs from 100 to 699.
tcf.mcq25: 25 questions that get harder as you go, and a right answer is worth more the later it comes. Your score runs from 100 to 499, and the level goes up to B2.
tcf.mcqEstimate: France Éducation international, which runs the TCF, does not publish its exact weights, so this score is an estimate.
tcf.mcqSlice: If you practised only some questions, you see how many you got right instead of a score.
tcf.prod: An AI examiner scores each task out of 20 on doing the task, organisation, vocabulary and grammar, plus fluency when you speak. Your section score is the average of your tasks.
tcf.nclc: Each skill's score becomes an NCLC level through IRCC's official table. Your overall level is your lowest skill.
tcf.cefr: Each skill gets a CEFR level, A1 to C2, from France Éducation international's official grid. Your overall level is your lowest skill.
tcf.quebecPoints: Next to each level you see the points Québec's immigration grid gives it. Points start at B2.
tcf.source: Sources: France Éducation international, Manuel du candidat; IRCC language test equivalency table.
tcf.sourceQuebec: Sources: France Éducation international, Manuel du candidat (April 2025); Québec's immigration points grid.
tcf.sourceIrn: Source: France Éducation international, Manuel du candidat (April 2025).

micAccess.deniedTitle: The system is blocking the microphone
micAccess.macStep1: Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Microphone.
micAccess.macStep2: Switch FlexiLingo on, then come back and press Try again. If it still fails, quit and reopen the app.
micAccess.winStep1: Open Settings, then Privacy & security, then Microphone.
micAccess.winStep2: Turn on microphone access, including "Let desktop apps access your microphone", then press Try again.
micAccess.otherStep1: Check your system sound settings and make sure an input device is selected and not muted.
micAccess.otherStep2: Allow FlexiLingo to use the microphone, then press Try again.
micAccess.openSettingsFailed: The settings page could not be opened. Open it from your system settings.
micAccess.noDevice: No microphone was found. Plug one in or choose an input device in your system settings, then try again.
micAccess.inUse: Another app is using the microphone. Close it, then try again.
micAccess.unsupported: This computer cannot record audio for the exam.
